newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel could oust Arafat over violence - official.
newsitem.headline: Israel could oust Arafat over violence - official.

text.p: Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi cautioned in remarks broadcast on Sunday that Israel could oust Palestinian President Yasser Arafat from the self-ruled Gaza Strip if violence erupted in the territories.
Hanegbi made the comment as Israel was set to begin as soon as Monday on construction of a new Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, a move the PLO has said could trigger widespread unrest.

"Whoever launches violence could very quickly find himself packing a suitcase and travelling back and forth on the line from Tunis to Baghdad like he (Arafat) did for many years," Hanegbi told supporters in the remarks on Saturday.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said he regretted Hanegbi's remarks. Hanegbi's counterpart in Arafat's Palestinian Authority cancelled a meeting with the Israeli minister following the speech.

"Arafat won't be able to sit in his villa on the beach with (his wife) Suha and give orders to act. There's no immunity for anyone wishing to annihilate us, neither for 'The Engineer' nor anyone in any villa," Hanegbi said.

"If war, then war to the end," he said. "The Engineer" was the code name of the master bomber Yahya Ayyash, responsible for suicide attacks of the Islamic militant group Hamas that killed scores of Israelis. Ayyash was killed in January 1996 when a mobile phone he held to his ear exploded in what was widely seen as an Israeli assassination.
